absent: Full layouts and ownership of cpufreq policy, governor attribute set, update utility data, runqueue, realtime and deadline runqueues, and clamp structures.
Numeric values and units of capacity scale, capacity shift, tick length, time conversion factors, and clamp identifiers.
Behavior of utilization mapping, frequency resolver, capacity and frequency scale helpers, and interrupt and realtime utilization trackers.
Governor registration, initialization, limit change handling, policy start and stop, and global tunables sharing discipline.
Driver fast switch, performance adjustment, target selection, and cross CPU update capability contracts.
Tickless idle call accounting, scheduler extension switching state, and CFS boost computation.
Complete worker thread lifecycle, affinity rules, error handling, and shutdown sequencing beyond creation.
Memory ordering guarantees beyond the single barrier pairing noted in the fragments.

findings.text: Tunables object pairs a generic governor attribute set with a single unsigned rate limit expressed in microseconds. The attribute set links the object into sysfs handling while the interval controls minimum spacing between frequency decisions.

Policy object holds a back pointer to the cpufreq policy plus a tunables pointer and list linkage, a raw spinlock guarding update state, last decision timestamp and minimum delay in nanoseconds, selected and cached frequencies, deferred work plumbing comprising interrupt work, threaded work, mutex, worker and thread pointer with a progress flag, and two flags recording limit changes and forced refresh need.

Per CPU object holds utilization callback state, owning policy pointer and CPU number, IO wait boost pending flag and level with last observation time, current utilization plus bandwidth floor and ceiling, and for single CPU policies an optional saved idle call counter when tickless idle accounting is enabled. Storage is a per CPU instance.
Minimum IO wait boost level is defined as one eighth of the scheduler capacity scale.
Global helper returns a reference frequency for a given cpufreq policy, used as baseline for utilization to frequency conversion.
Global helper derives an effective performance target from actual utilization with headroom mapping, clamped between caller supplied floor and ceiling and never exceeding the mapped actual.
Global helper computes effective CPU utilization from CFS input plus realtime and deadline contributions with interrupt scaling, optionally reporting bandwidth floor and ceiling.
Global helper applies scheduler attributes without access checks by delegating to the internal scheduler setter with unchecked flags.
Configured microsecond interval is converted to a signed nanosecond delay using widened arithmetic so large values do not overflow on narrow word sizes.

Frequency decision is skipped when the local CPU cannot act on the policy, forced when limits changed or a forced refresh is pending, otherwise allowed only after the configured delay has elapsed since the prior decision.

New selection is stored with its timestamp only when it differs from the prior selection or a forced refresh is active, with an extra driver flag controlling whether identical values after limit changes still trigger an update.
Slow path notification queues interrupt work exactly once until the worker clears the progress flag, preventing duplicate queueing.
Reference frequency prefers an architecture supplied reference, then the policy maximum when frequency invariance is available, otherwise the current frequency inflated by one quarter as headroom.
Raw frequency derived from utilization mapping is cached; if unchanged and no forced refresh is pending the prior selection is reused without consulting the driver resolver.

Per CPU utilization sampling starts from scheduler extension target plus CFS boost when not fully switched, passes through effective utilization to obtain floor and ceiling, raises the result by any IO boost, then applies performance mapping and stores all three outputs.

Effective utilization saturates at capacity when interrupt pressure alone fills the CPU, otherwise sums CFS, realtime and deadline parts, derives minimum from interrupt plus deadline bandwidth versus clamp floor with special maximum handling for runnable realtime without clamps, derives maximum from clamp ceiling, and rescales task part to account for hidden interrupt time before adding it back.
Realtime runnability requires both queued and running counts nonzero; deadline bandwidth converts running bandwidth to capacity scale by fixed shift.

IO boost state resets only after more than one tick has elapsed since last update, installing either minimum level or zero depending on whether the current event is an IO wakeup, and reports whether a reset occurred.

IO boost first attempts timed reset when a level exists, ignores non IO events, ensures doubling happens at most once per request via a pending flag, doubles existing levels up to capacity scale, and seeds first IO wakeup at minimum.

Applied boost is zero when no level exists or a timed reset fires, otherwise halves the stored level when no request is pending and disables levels falling below minimum, clears pending, and rescales the level into current capacity.

Single policy hold heuristic is bypassed for fully switched extension schedulers and for clamp capped runqueues, otherwise it preserves frequency when idle entry count has not advanced since last check, updating the saved count each time; an alternate build always declines to hold.
When current deadline bandwidth exceeds the last stored floor, a forced refresh flag is set so deadline demand bypasses normal interval throttling.
Common single policy path updates IO boost state and timestamp, checks deadline bypass, applies gating, then samples boost and utilization, returning whether the caller should proceed to selection.

Single frequency path uses CPU capacity as scale, aborts when common preparation declines, selects via utilization mapping, optionally retains prior frequency when hold suggests reduction is premature while restoring cached raw value, then either fast switches directly or queues deferred work under lock when the selection changed.

Single performance path falls back to frequency handling without invariance, otherwise follows common preparation and hold logic on utilization levels, then programs bandwidth floor, target and ceiling through the driver performance interface and clears forced refresh while stamping time.

Shared policy selection scans every CPU in the policy, applies per CPU IO boost and refreshes utilization, retains the largest target across members, and maps that peak to a frequency using the invoking CPU capacity.

Shared update callback serializes the whole decision under the policy raw spinlock, performs IO boost and deadline handling, and on gating success selects peak frequency and either fast switches or defers.
Single policy frequency and performance callbacks serve as utilization hooks, extracting per CPU state from the generic hook container and driving their respective selection paths.
Threaded work handler snapshots the selected frequency and clears progress under lock before invoking the driver target under mutex; interrupt work handler forwards to threaded work queue.
Rate limit attribute exposes current microseconds on read and on write parses a new value, updates shared tunables and propagates converted delays to every policy linked to the attribute set.
Tunables objects are released by freeing the container derived from the attribute set, with a kernel object type binding default groups, sysfs operations and release handler.

Policy allocation zero initializes storage, links the cpufreq policy and initializes the update lock, with a matching free; a governor object is declared; a deadline attributed worker thread is created only for non fast switch policies, with affinity constrained to related CPUs and interrupt work plus mutex initialized before wakeup.

Per CPU update path relies on runqueue lock serialization for the target CPU, avoiding extra locking for fast switch; shared decisions and deferred queueing hold the policy raw spinlock, while threaded application uses irq safe variant for snapshot plus a dedicated mutex for driver invocation.

IO boost cycles among idle zero, seeded minimum, doubled growth capped at capacity, halved decay when idle, and timed reset after a tick, with a pending flag ensuring single doubling per wakeup and cleared on application.

Frequency control moves from gated idle through forced refresh on limit change or deadline growth to selection caching and commit, with slow path adding queued interrupt work to threaded driver application and progress flag preventing requeue until consumed.

Narrow arithmetic could overflow without widening, limit flag clearing must precede limit reads with a barrier paired to the updater, cross CPU requests without hardware support must be dropped, and offline CPUs must not leave stale interrupt work behind.

Threaded snapshot must hold the update lock briefly or a concurrent selection arriving between read and progress clear could be lost; hold logic must not override clamp limits or extension scheduler targets.
A file scoped tunables pointer and a file scoped mutex exist for global tunables management.
